title: TARGET vs APPROVED BLOCKOUT vs STRUCTURAL FRAME WITH ROCK/TERRAIN

target.required_read: Broad continuous cliff platform, two clearly separated levels, controlled natural rock silhouette, large/medium rock facets, subdued terrain material supporting architecture.

approved_blockout.evidence: VALORIA ART PRODUCTION RESET v1 approved seven-camera blockout
approved_blockout.strengths: Correct composition, screen occupancy, level anchors and route/architecture placement.
approved_blockout.weakness: Structural terrain reads as flat technical slabs/dark cliff bands plus seven explicit shoulder proxies; insufficient authored geological identity.

structural_frame_source08.result: The same macro envelope is retained while the visible plateau and upper rise become continuous faceted rock masses with distinct earth planes. Seven shoulder proxies disappear into the geological mass instead of repeating as supports.
structural_frame_source08.quantitative: All 63 protected non-terrain elements/view are exactly 0 px delta. Rock/Terrain macro width/height differs from blockout by less than 0.00002% in every official view; center shift is below 0.0001 px.
structural_frame_source08.visual_jump: YES — this is a frame-level improvement, not a local polish pass. The accepted gate/bridge/road/stair now sit on authored terrain rather than greybox support geometry.
structural_frame_source08.remaining_gap: The overall frame is not final target quality because Walls, Bastion, Cabin/Camp, Vegetation, Props, Water/Shore and Background remain intentionally outside this block. Their greybox/placeholder state must not be counted against Rock/Terrain.

conclusion: PASS — Rock/Terrain materially closes the target gap while preserving composition. It produces the first major global-frame transformation in this family sequence without moving accepted architecture or gameplay.
